**Chunk 1 – Summary of the General Design‑Criteria Sections (Pages 25‑30)** | **Section / Topic** | **Key Measurable Requirements, Dimensions, Loads, Limits & Conditions** | |---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **1.1 Introduction** | • Scope: all civil‑engineering works for the Land Transport Authority (LTA).
• Definitions follow the contract conditions.
• “Engineer” = the Authority‑appointed Engineer or Superintending Officer. | | **1.1.3 General Obligations** | • **Statutory compliance** – designs must be signed off by a Professional Engineer (PE) with a valid practising certificate (PEA) and an Accredited Checker (Building Control Act).
• Must meet the Building Control Act, Fire Safety Act and any relevant Singapore (SS) or British (BS) standards – **no legal immunity** from meeting those statutes.
• Designs must consider **adjacent works** (existing & planned services) and any constraints they impose. | | **1.2 Standards** | • Primary references: **Singapore Standards (SPRING)**; if none, use **British Standards (BSI)**; if still none, a reputable standard may be used with Engineer’s approval (three English copies required).
• Metric versions prevail over imperial.
• **BS 5400** is the baseline for bridges, applied as amended by the UK Highways Agency (UHA) manuals and by this Design Criteria.
• Specific UHA Design Manual documents (BD 15/92, 16/82, 20/92, 24/92, 30/87, 32/88, 33/94, 36/92, 37/01, 52/93, 60/94, 49/01, 31/01, etc.) are incorporated unless the Criteria state otherwise. | | **1.3 Design** | **1.3.1 Responsibility** – staff with proven relevant experience must carry out design and detailing.
**1.3.2 Design Objectives** – structures must be **safe, robust, economical, durable, low‑maintenance, fit‑for‑purpose, simple in form, and aesthetically pleasing**.
**Durability target:** **120 years service life** for all permanent structures (with appropriate maintenance).
**Limit‑state requirement:** All structural designs must satisfy **ultimate** and **serviceability** limit states. | | **1.3.3 Temporary Works** | • Must be compatible with permanent works and **endorsed by a PE**.
• Any permanent element that serves a temporary function is to be analysed for **both permanent and temporary conditions**; the more onerous condition governs. | | **1.3.4 Design for Removal of Temporary Works** | • **All temporary works shall be designed for removal**.
• Exception: contractor may propose to leave works in place (Engineer approval required).
• Removal must **not damage permanent works**.
• **Void‑filling:** any void left after removal must be filled **immediately with grout** (grout mix & method to be approved).
• If left in‑ground, design must prevent settlement or decay effects (e.g., timber decay).
• **Depth limit for retained works:** must be **≤ 2 m below finished ground level** (unless Authority drawings state otherwise). This applies also to secant piles, diaphragm walls, etc. | | **1.3.5 Oversite & Adjacent Development** | Design must be **independent of any benefit** from oversite or neighbouring development; the design shall assume the worst‑case (e.g., no adjacent support) for stability, flotation, lateral loading, etc. | | **1.3.6 Structure Gauge** | All movable equipment, hinged doors, windows, covers to sumps/pits, etc., **must not intrude into the Structure Gauge** at any position of movement. | | **1.4 Calculations** | • Calculations must follow **current applicable standards** (unless later chapters specify otherwise).
• **State‑of‑the‑art** or unproven methods are prohibited without Engineer’s prior acceptance.
• **Computer programs** may be used only if **approved by the Engineer**; they must be from reputable vendors, fully tested, and proven on similar projects.
• Required documentation: sample calculations, program assumptions, limitations, and a clear design statement.
• For in‑house spreadsheets: submit the exact version, full formula print‑out, and hand‑calculation verification for all scenarios. | | **1.4.3 Units** | **Metric (SI) units** are mandatory; where both metric and imperial versions of a standard exist, the metric version controls. | ### Quick Reference of Measurable Items | Item | Value / Requirement | |------|----------------------| | Service life (durability) | **120 years** (permanent structures) | | Removal depth for retained temporary works | **≤ 2 m** below finished ground level | | Limit‑state compliance | **Ultimate & serviceability** must be satisfied | | Design endorsement | Must be signed by a **Professional Engineer** (and Accredited Checker where required) | | Standards hierarchy | **Singapore (SPRING) → British (BSI) → other reputable standard (Engineer approval)** | | Units | **SI (metric) only** | These points capture the **section topics**, the **quantifiable or limit‑based requirements**, the **dimensional constraints**, the **load‑related references**, and the **conditions** under which the civil works must be designed, detailed, and verified.

**Chunk 2 – Summary of Design‑Criteria Highlights** | **Section / Topic** | **Key Measurable Requirements & Limits** | **Dimensions / Values** | **Loads / Environmental Conditions** | **Special Conditions / Notes** | |---------------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------| | **1.4 Units & Language** | • All calculations in SI (BS 3763).
• Stress expressed as **N / mm²** or **kN / m²**.
• Documents submitted in **English**. | – | – | – | | **1.5 Survey & Setting‑out** | • Levels referenced to a **Project datum 100 m below Singapore Land Authority Precise Levelling Datum (PLD)**.
• All plan coordinates must use the **project coordinate system** defined in the Particular Specification and shown on the drawings. | – | – | Coordinate system must be clearly indicated on every drawing. | | **1.6 Durability Assurance** | • Design must prove durability for the whole service life.
• Concrete, metal corrosion, sealants, waterproofing, coatings, etc., must be assessed for the exposure environment (e.g., ground‑water).
• Critical elements (inaccessible for maintenance) must remain durable **without any maintenance**; optional instrumentation for performance monitoring. | – | Exposure to ground water, aggressive soils, etc. | • Durability assessment must consider: micro‑environment, deterioration mechanisms, likely material life, monitoring/maintenance feasibility, cost‑effectiveness of extra protection, significance of deterioration.
• Concrete quality‑control tests and acceptance criteria must be supplied. | | **1.6.4 Life‑Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA)** | • Perform LCCA when required to select materials.
• Include **initial capital cost**, **total recurrent cost** (inspection, monitoring, maintenance/repair), and **replacement cost**.
• Express total life‑cycle cost as **Net Present Value (NPV)** using a **5 % discount rate**.
• Conduct a **sensitivity analysis** for uncertainties in material performance, workmanship, and unit rates. | – | – | LCCA is a decision‑making tool; accuracy needed only for comparative purposes. | | **1.6.5 Concrete Design Data** | • On design drawings, clearly show:
 – **Design characteristic strength**
 – **Maximum nominal aggregate size**
 – **Minimum cement content**
 – **Maximum cement content**
 – **Maximum water‑cement ratio**
 – **Permitted cement types**. | – | – | Applies to reinforced, precast, and prestressed concrete works. | | **1.6.6 Drawings** | • Drawings must follow **Drawing & CAD Standard (MicroStation)** and **SS CP83**. | – | – | – | | **1.7 Materials & Workmanship Specification** | • Spec is a **minimum standard**; any incompatibility with the design must be highlighted and agreed with the Engineer. | – | – | – | | **1.8 Dimensions** | • All dimensions on Authority drawings are **minimums**; actual on‑site dimensions must accommodate construction tolerances, wall deflection, beam/floor sag, etc. | – | – | – | | **1.9 Concrete Blinding** | • Blinding concrete **minimum grade C15** and **minimum thickness 50 mm**.
• Thickness/strength may be increased for soft/irregular ground or large pours.
• If the ground beneath blinding will later be removed, a **debonding membrane** must be placed at the interface. | **C15**, **≥ 50 mm** | – | Blinding details must appear on design drawings. | | **1.10 Land Boundaries & Use** | • Design must respect existing land boundaries; avoid encroachment.
• Railway works: State land is preferred; non‑State land only as a **last resort** and must be accessible from State land.
• Road works: Built on State land; non‑State land only as a last resort (Street Works Act).
• Layout must avoid creating unusable “remnant” parcels. | – | – | Any proposal that would require permanent acquisition of non‑State land may be rejected. | | **1.11 Flood Protection** | • **Design Flood Level (DFL)** = **1 m above the highest recorded flood level** (per PUB/Drainage).
• All openings (entrances, vent shafts, tunnel portals, service entries, road thresholds, under‑passes, etc.) must be **≥ DFL**.
• Drainage/sewer discharge points must have **swan‑neck** or gravity exit **above DFL** to prevent back‑flow.
• **Platform & crest level**: platform ≥ DFL; threshold ≥ 150 mm **above platform** (crest).
• Adjacent developments must meet the same DFL and crest‑level requirements. | **DFL = Highest recorded flood + 1 m**
**Crest ≥ 150 mm above platform** | Flood water level (design condition). | All flood‑protection measures must satisfy PUB (Drainage) requirements. | | **2.1 RTS Alignment – General** | • Track‑alignment design must meet functional requirements of this chapter and consider all relevant criteria (operation, safety, etc.). | – | – | This is the introductory statement for the alignment chapter (details follow in later sections). | ### Quick‑Reference Checklist - **Units**: SI only; stress N / mm² or kN / m². - **Language**: English. - **Vertical datum**: Project datum = PLD – 100 m. - **Coordinate system**: Project‑specific, shown on every drawing. - **Durability**: Full life‑cycle assessment; critical elements must be maintenance‑free; provide monitoring where possible. - **LCCA**: Use 5 % discount rate; include capital, recurrent, and replacement costs; run sensitivity analysis. - **Concrete**: Minimum blinding C15, ≥ 50 mm thick; design drawings must list all concrete mix limits. - **Land use**: Prefer State land; non‑State land only as last resort; respect cadastral boundaries. - **Flood protection**: DFL = highest flood + 1 m; openings ≥ DFL; platform threshold ≥ 150 mm above platform; drainage exits above DFL. These points capture the measurable, dimensional, load‑related, limit, and conditional requirements presented in Chunk 2 of the Civil Design Criteria document.
